title: Works vs Physical Services under PPR 2025
text:
Under the Public Procurement Rules (PPR) 2025, enacted by the Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority (BPPA), public procurement is organised into distinct categories. The key difference between Works and Physical Services is whether the contract requires constructing or modifying a tangible structure, or delivering routine operational tasks.

Direct Comparison








Feature
Works
Physical Services (non-consulting)




Core objective
Construction, civil engineering, rehabilitation or physical modification of a facility or asset.
Operational, transactional or routine support tasks that are measurable but do not result in structural building.


Nature of output
Tangible built infrastructure (roads, buildings, water supplies, bridges).
Execution of a continuous or standalone activity (security, cleaning, logistics).


Standard documents
Standard e-Tender Documents for Works (e.g. e-PW3).
Standard e-Tender Documents for Physical Services (e.g. e-PPS3, e-PPS6).


Examples
Building a bridge or highway; constructing school buildings; major pipe installation or tube well development.
Outsourced janitorial, catering or security services; ICT data collection, training and testing; operations and maintenance (O&M) of existing facilities.





Works (Civil and Engineering Projects)

Definition: executing construction or repair projects that involve engineering designs, physical site development and capital investment.
Rule change: a notable update to the national Works framework is the removal of the ±10% price cap under the Open Tendering Method (OTM), to improve market compliance.
Evaluation: bids are assessed heavily on performance security, compliance with technical drawings, structural engineering capability and financial capability.



Physical Services (Non-Consulting Services)

Definition: action-based tasks that need physical execution but involve no building or construction. They are distinct from Intellectual/Consulting Services, which focus on mental expertise, policy or advisory work.
Separate classification: PPR 2025 recognises Physical Services as a standalone procurement category. This stops procuring entities from forcing routine maintenance or outsourcing into Goods or Works template contracts.
Evaluation: monitored through Activity Schedules and Performance Specifications, using specialised e-GP templates. Significantly low-priced tenders (SLT) are screened out using a standard deviation formula, to protect worker wages and service standards.



A Quick Rule of Thumb
Ask what the contract leaves behind. If the answer is a built or modified asset, it is Works. If the answer is a service performed over time, with nothing structural left at the end, it is Physical Services.


Sources

BPPA news item on PPR 2025
BPPA standard document e-PPS3
e-GP portal
Understanding procurement nature: goods, works, services (LinkedIn)







Note



This post summarises secondary sources. Check the current PPR 2025 text and the relevant standard tender document before drafting a specification.

title: NCT vs ICT Tendering in Bangladesh
text:
In Bangladesh public procurement, under the Electronic Standard Tender Documents (eSTDs) on e-GP and the Public Procurement Rules, NCT (National Competitive Tendering) and ICT (International Competitive Tendering) are the two main methods for inviting bids. The choice depends on the geographic scope, value and technical complexity of the contract.






Warning



Here ICT means International Competitive Tendering. It is unrelated to the ICT Division (Information and Communication Technology), which is mentioned further down as a place to find tech tenders.



Key Differences








Feature
NCT (National)
ICT (International)




Participant scope
Local suppliers, contractors or consultants within Bangladesh
Global and domestic suppliers and contractors


Bidding language
Typically the local language (Bangla)
English (and/or the local language)


Market competition
Domestic market only
International market


Timeline
Shorter bidding and processing windows
Longer, because of international advertising, shipping and clarification rules


Bidder cost and complexity
Lower cost, low regulatory complexity
Higher cost and complexity: foreign exchange, international law, multi-currency terms


Typical use
Routine goods, small-to-medium works, local services
Specialised goods, high-value contracts, technology-intensive or large infrastructure projects





Where to Find and Manage Tenders

e-GP portal: the official electronic government procurement platform, where both NCT and ICT packages are published.
Line ministries and departments: bodies such as the ICT Division and the Department of ICT regularly post e-tender notices for technology tools, network installation and consultancy.
Aggregators: sites like BDTender collect active notices from the ICT ministry and related sectors.



Choosing Between Them
Start with who can realistically supply the item. If the local market can deliver at fair value, NCT is faster and cheaper for everyone. If the item is specialised or high-value enough that foreign suppliers are needed for real competition, ICT is the route, at the price of a longer timeline and heavier bidder paperwork.

e-GP portal
